name: Koh Ker embankment and road
summary: A seven-kilometre earthen embankment at Koh Ker that dammed a valley to form a reservoir and carried a road on its crest; it probably failed soon after building.
description: Approximately 7 km earthen embankment across the Stung Rongea valley, forming a reservoir and carrying an access route on its crest.
tier_reason: A bounded technical contribution, transmission episode or documented configuration useful within a specific history; no broad dependence claim is established.

date.label: by c. 950 CE (inferred)
date.basis: The authors date construction probably 928–941 CE and model likely failure within roughly a decade; the broad upper horizon is approximate.

events.statement: The embankment is interpreted as storing river water and providing a crest route linking Koh Ker with the highway before the hypothesized breach.
events.population: Koh Ker builders and users of the capital’s road and water infrastructure
events.caveats: Water storage and crest-route function are archaeological interpretations; named users, unrestricted access, complete commissioning and individual operating dates are not proved. Probable construction and early failure are model-based estimates.

evidence.supports: Describes the capital-period weir, roadway, spillway and chute.

events.caveats: The date, failure sequence and wider consequences are hypotheses, not an eyewitness account or an exact date of total abandonment.
